title: Jacksonville opens Forsyth & Adams Streets for two-way traffic | Duval Times
text:
Donna Deegan - Mayor of Jacksonville, FL | City of Jacksonville website
Donna Deegan - Mayor of Jacksonville, FL | City of Jacksonville website
The city of Jacksonville has reopened Forsyth and Adams Streets to two-way traffic, a change aimed at fostering economic growth, increasing property values, supporting small businesses, and optimizing the use of on-street parking and rideshare services.
"This marks a major milestone in our vision to revitalize Downtown," stated Jacksonville Mayor Donna Deegan. "We’re bringing back walkability and foot traffic, slowing down vehicular traffic, and creating spaces where people want to gather and spend some time, rather than just speed through on their way someplace else."
The announcement signifies the completion of the first phase of the project, which involved signal upgrades, pavement markings, and two-way re-striping. Future plans include expanded sidewalks, green tree canopies, and enhanced streetscapes as part of efforts to reinvigorate the city's core according to the Downtown master plan.
Forsyth and Adams Streets were originally two-way until they were converted in the late 1930s during a period that prioritized car movement over pedestrian access. The reintroduction of two-way streets has been a longstanding goal within Jacksonville's Downtown master plan. It is supported by Mobility Plan Updates and transportation projects with funding from the Downtown Investment Authority.
Benefits expected from this change include improved retail visibility and occupancy rates, enhanced walkability and pedestrian safety, increased sidewalk activity, as well as elevated residential demand and quality of life.
